# ggplot Review

```{r}
ebola_data <- read_excel('data/Ebola_Sierra Leone.xlsx') %>% 
    mutate(age_group = case_when(
        age < 18 ~ 'minor',
        age >= 18 & age < 65 ~ "adult",
        age >= 65 ~ 'senior'
    ),
    sex       = factor(sex, labels = c('female', 'male')),
    status    = factor(status, labels = c('negative', 'positive')),
    age_group = factor(age_group, levels = c('minor', 'adult', 'senior') )
    ) 

ebola_data
```

## Histograms

```{r}
ebola_data %>% 
    ggplot(aes(x = age)) +
    geom_histogram(fill = 'orange', color = 'black') +
    labs(title = 'Age Distribution',
         x = 'Age',
         y = 'Count') +
    theme_minimal()
    
```

## Boxplots

```{r}
ebola_data %>% 
    drop_na(sex) %>% 
    ggplot(aes(y = age, x = sex, fill = sex)) +
    geom_boxplot() +
    labs(title = 'Age Distribution by Sex',
         x     = 'Sex',
         y     = 'Age') +
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(legend.position = 'none',
          plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5))
```

## Epicurves

```{r}
epicurve_data <- ebola_data %>% 
    filter(status == "positive") %>% 
    group_by(date_of_onset) %>% 
    summarise(count = n())

epicurve_data
```

```{r}

epicurve_data %>% 
    ggplot(aes(x = date_of_onset, y = count)) +
    geom_col(fill = 'darkgreen') +
    labs(title = 'New Cases by Day',
         x     = 'Date of Onset',
         y     = 'Cases') +
    theme_minimal()
    
```

```{r}
epicurve_data <- ebola_data %>% 
    drop_na(sex) %>% 
    filter(status == "positive") %>% 
    group_by(district, date_of_onset) %>% 
    summarise(count = n())

epicurve_data %>% 
    ggplot(aes(x = date_of_onset, y = count)) +
    geom_col(fill = 'darkgreen') +
    labs(title = 'New Cases by Day',
         x     = 'Date of Onset',
         y     = 'Cases') +
    theme_minimal() +
    facet_wrap(~district)
```

# Proportion and Frequency Tables

## CrossTable

```{r}

CrossTable(ebola_data$age_group, ebola_data$status, chisq = TRUE)
```

## freq()

```{r}
ebola_data %>% 
    select(sex, age, district, chiefdom, age_group) %>% 
    freq()
```

# Bivariate Analysis

```{r}
status_agegroup <- glm(status ~ age_group, 
                       family = binomial("logit"), 
                       data = ebola_data)

status_agegroup
```

```{r}
exp(cbind(OR = coef(status_agegroup), confint(status_agegroup)))
```

```{r}
epitools::oddsratio(ebola_data$age_group,  ebola_data$status)
```

# Multivariate Analysis

```{r}
status_age_sex <- glm(status ~ age + sex, 
                      family = binomial('logit'), 
                      data = ebola_data)

status_age_sex
```

```{r}
exp(cbind(OR = coef(status_age_sex), confint(status_age_sex)))
```

```{r}
sex_by_status <- table(ebola_data$sex, ebola_data$status)
sex_by_status
```

```{r}
epiR::epi.2by2(sex_by_status, method = "cohort.count")
```

# Survival Analysis

```{r}
# Install once if needed
# install.packages(c("tidyverse", "lubridate", "survival", "survminer", "broom"))

library(tidyverse)
library(lubridate)
library(survival)
library(survminer)
library(broom)

# 1) READ DATA ---------------------------------------------------------------

# Replace the path if needed
df_raw <- readr::read_csv("data/Ebola_Simulated.csv",
                          show_col_types = FALSE)

# Peek
glimpse(df_raw)

# Expected columns in this file:
# case_id, generation, date_of_infection, date_of_onset, date_of_hospitalisation,
# date_of_outcome, outcome (0=recovered, 1=death), gender (0/1), hospital, longitude, latitude

# 2) CLEAN & BUILD SURVIVAL OBJECT ------------------------------------------

df <- df_raw %>%
  mutate(
    # Parse dates
    date_of_onset  = ymd(date_of_onset),
    date_of_outcome = ymd(date_of_outcome),

    # Event indicator: death = 1, otherwise censored
    status = case_when(
      outcome == 1 ~ 1L,                 # died
      TRUE ~ 0L                           # recovered or unknown -> treat as censored
    ),

    # Time origin: symptom onset (you can change the origin if your question differs)
    # Time-to-event in DAYS
    time = as.numeric(difftime(date_of_outcome, date_of_onset, units = "days"))
  ) %>%
  # Keep rows with a defined onset and non-negative time
  filter(!is.na(date_of_onset), !is.na(time), time >= 0) %>%
  mutate(
    gender = factor(gender, levels = c(0,1), labels = c("Female","Male")),
    hospital = factor(hospital),                 # treat as categorical site indicator
    generation = as.integer(generation)
  )

summary(df$time)
table(df$status, useNA = "ifany")
table(df$gender, useNA = "ifany")

```

```{r}
# Survival object
surv_obj <- Surv(time = df$time, event = df$status)

# 2a) Overall KM -------------------------------------------------------------
fit_km_overall <- survfit(surv_obj ~ 1, data = df)
summary(fit_km_overall)

# 2b) KM by gender -----------------------------------------------------------
fit_km_gender <- survfit(surv_obj ~ gender, data = df)
summary(fit_km_gender)

# 2c) Log-rank test (gender) -------------------------------------------------
logrank_gender <- survdiff(surv_obj ~ gender, data = df)
logrank_gender
broom::tidy(logrank_gender)  # gives chisq and p-value in a tidy tibble

```

```{r}
# Start with a simple model
cox1 <- coxph(surv_obj ~ gender, data = df)
summary(cox1)

# Add additional covariates (example: generation and hospital as categorical site)
# Only include covariates that are well-populated (few NAs) and make clinical sense.
cox2 <- coxph(surv_obj ~ gender + generation + hospital, data = df)
summary(cox2)

# Tidy outputs with hazard ratios and CIs
tidy_cox2 <- broom::tidy(cox2, exponentiate = TRUE, conf.int = TRUE)
tidy_cox2

```

```{r}
# Grambsch–Therneau test for PH assumption
ph_test <- cox.zph(cox2)
ph_test
plot(ph_test)  # diagnostic plots; look for no strong trends in residuals over time

```

```{r}
# 5a) KM curve: overall ------------------------------------------------------
p_overall <- ggsurvplot(
  fit_km_overall,
  data = df,
  conf.int = TRUE,
  risk.table = TRUE,
  xlab = "Days since symptom onset",
  ylab = "Survival probability",
  title = "Overall Kaplan–Meier Survival",
  ggtheme = theme_minimal(base_size = 13)
)
p_overall

# 5b) KM stratified by gender -----------------------------------------------
p_gender <- ggsurvplot(
  fit_km_gender,
  data = df,
  conf.int = TRUE,
  risk.table = TRUE,
  pval = TRUE,                 # shows log-rank p-value
  xlab = "Days since symptom onset",
  ylab = "Survival probability",
  title = "Kaplan–Meier Survival by Gender",
  legend.title = "Gender",
  ggtheme = theme_minimal(base_size = 13)
)
p_gender

```
